Citrusdal floods

By: Catherine Rice | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Citrusdal town cut off from world as Western Cape floods wreak havoc

Unique Selling Point:
Citrusdal, a farming town in the Olifants River Valley in the Western Cape, was cut off from the world as devastating floods washed away their main access road after heavy rains hit the area between 14 and 19 June. During that time there was no way in, and no way out. The area was also without electricity after utility poles supporting overhead power lines collapsed. The town is home to around five thousand people and is dominated by citrus farming.

Summary:
The town is in a race against time as they are in the middle of harvesting - this means they need trucks with access to farms in order to get the fruit packed and transported out. With the R303 entrance road washed away, the only access point is now a low lying bridge crossing (opened for trucks on June 21). However, it can only be used as a temporary measure, while engineers work around the clock to repair the washed away main access point. Initial damage to the agricultural industry in the province is currently between R750million and a billion rand. Thousands of people in the province have been displaced from their homes, and two people have died during the flooding. Citrusdal was the hardest hit in the region, and relief efforts were difficult with no access to the town for several days. Gift of the Givers have been providing essential items, like blankets and non-perishable foods. The SANDF provided a helicopter to ferry Eskom officials in to restore electricity after five days without it. Gift of the Givers is also visiting the area on Monday to provide donations and food to the stricken community.

Further information:
Abrie Van Zyl is one of the farmers who has been financially devastated by the floods. He planted orchards on 28 hectares in September last year. They have all been destroyed and he believes his financial losses run into the millions. He has invested all of his personal savings into the project, and is not sure he will be able to recover from this. He is trying to save the fully grown orchards he has, and is working around the clock to harvest what he can. More rains are expected next week, with four days predicted from Tuesday to Friday. Farmers say this is the worst flooding they have had in forty years.

Extra Budget Items:
Cost of an overnight stay in Citrusdal and car travel from Cape Town.

Riaan Carstens

Script:


VO 1 It’s the middle of June...…

VO 2 Cold fronts grip the Western Cape… one after the other…

NATSOUND let it breathe (Greg got nice shots of the rain, close up shots etc)

VO 3 The heavens open, battering the region….

(Cellphone visuals of the floods) NATSOUND

VO 4 In the Olifants River Valley, at the foot of the majestic Cederberg… five days of rain pelt the town of Citrusdal.

VO 5 Farmers brace themselves after word reaches them…from up in the valley.

VOICE NOTE 1: I've seen Olifants in places I have never seen it flow in my lifetime. So yes there at the town a problem is coming (voice note)

VISUAL DRAMA & NATSOUND

VO 6 All too soon the ever-steady Olifantsriver… becomes a raging torrent…a relentless…unstoppable…driving force wiping out everything in its path

VO 7 The main access road washes away

VO 8 Nearby …. Clanwilliam Dam soon reaches capacity ….the sluice gates are opened claiming construction offices ….ripping away their makeshift foundations …

MORE NATSOUND more viz of offices flowing down river.

VOICE NOTE And it's growing all the time. It's getting stronger all the time. (from the second voice note)

VISUAL DRAMA & NATSOUND

VO 9 The flood continues undeterred, water levels keep rising -.......the town is cut off.

BIG PAUSE

VO 10 The SANDF flies in Eskom technicians to restore power.

VO 11 Rainfall in June is a given, but this is something else…

CELLPHONE FOOTAGE UP TO THIS POINT.

TRANSITION TO QUIET / CUT TO BLACK

Abrie van Zyl Farmer Clip 4494 Time code 00:49
I am the fourth generation and yes I am at this stage I am under my mother, who is the owner of the farm.

VO 12 Orange farmer Abrie van Zyl was one of those bracing for trouble down in the valley.

VO 13 As the river rises, his anxiety increases..

UPSOUND SUBTITLES Abrie van Zyl / Farmer Clip 4494 Time code 00:01:51 Reports came through that this is the highest they’ve ever seen the river. People who are up to fifty, sixty years old, and grew up their whole life in Citrusdal, this immediately told us, here comes trouble. If those types of men tell you that it’s the highest they’ve ever seen it in their lives, then yes, its a lot of water. End code 02:23:28

VO 14 And they were right.

(Silent….Visuals of him walking around his decimated orchards / drone visuals.)

VO 15 His entire life savings has been invested in 28 hectares of newly planted orchards - an estimated ten million rand… obliterated by the river’s mighty current.

VO 16 In the face of the overflowing river, Abrie is helpless.

UPSOUND: Abrie van Zyl (subtitles) Clip 4495 Time code: 00:00:26 I physically stood on the embankment to stop the water. At that time I was standing in the orchard and saw how the water was coming over the embankment.That was for me the hardest moment to see and to know that you’ve done what you can, but Mother Nature has decided.

UPSOUND Abrie van Zyl Destroys a man’s dreams and sets a person back a good few years.

VO 17 What no-one here forgets is that only five years ago farmers were fighting over scarce water allocations from this river…amid the most sever drought in living memory in the Western Cape …

VO 18 Further down the valley, the flood reaches the informal settlement, Riverview. Anele Njameni is a seasonal farmworker. He was forced to flee to safety when the rains came.

UPSOUND (will provide time codes on Tuesday) Clip 4606 Time code: 03:35 Anele Njameni / Flood victim “I woke up, I looked outside, my neighbour was outside of the house and water was coming inside of the house, and the house is moving, I ended up packing and going out with one bag.

VO 19 With no shelter, he seeks refuge in the community hall with several hundred others

ERIN PRESENTER LINK places like Riverview have been flattened by the flood and the Cederberg Munipality is taking steps to have Citrusdal and nearby flood hit areas declared a disaster which would bring much needed relief funds from government.
NATSOUND Anele showing Erin where his house once stood.

VO 20 A no work no pay policy means seasonal farmworkers like Anele are desperate to get back to the orchards.

UPSOUND ANELE clip 4606 / Time code 01:13 It’s been three weeks without something coming in as income so its been bad, really bad. And then now the employers, people who give us work, they have lost stuff, the trees, everything destroyed.

BREATHE HERE WITH VISUALS

VO 21 It’s Wednesday, the 21st of June, one week after the rains started. The low lying bridge is finally able to be used again as the water recedes.

VO 22 This low-lying bridge which is privately owned is being used as an interim measure. It had to be reinforced for trucks, laden with produce. Trucks HAVE TO get in and out - it’s harvest time.. And they’re behind.

VO 23 Local resident Riaan Carstens, steps in to co-ordinate the safe crossing of trucks in and out of the area over the low lying bridge..

NATSOUND Erin: I’m a bit nervous to drive across here. Riaan: This should be fine, its only when water goes over cement blocks.

UPSOUND RIAAN CARSTENS / CITRUSDAL Community policing forum Clip 4574 Time code: 05:20 We’ve gone through this a couple of times, you know there’s a flood coming and everyone is prepared for it. It was only when people realised its a lot worse than ever before, people start panic buying, milk and bread run out, we have seasonal workers, when cash runs out, they really in a bind, gas started running out.

ERIN: PRESENTER LINK: Floods last cut off the town in 1984, but locals say this time round is way worse. AND. Engineers are working around the clock to rebuild the main access road.

VO 24 The disaster has triggered local memories of previous floods…an old family film from the 1960s has survived to tell the story.

(old visuals of 1960s visuals, COURTESY STRAP: Koffie Matthee).

VO 25 Johan Burger is a truck driver, who’s lived in Citrusdal almost his entire life. When he was a young man, the access road washed away as well.

UPSPOUND: Johan Burger / Truck Driver
…Time code 000:3:30 Clip 4627 SUBTITLES Even in 1984, the road washed away,, but this year’s flood was much worse. It’s the first time I’ve seen it like that as long as I’ve lived in the valley. Clip 4628 Time code: 00:01:59 At that time you saw, they were busy there the farmers and I also helped, we had to fasten ropes and we brought the most needy people this side. (photo of wooden row boats) Clip 4628 Time code 00: 02:04 So I helped because they had a rowing boat that they fastened with ropes.

VO 26 In these floods, updated methods ….. But the same terrror (visuals of the rubber tire)

VO 27 Now, as extreme weather events become more frequent, more intense - the climate change crisis….hits the most vulnerable first

VO 28 And while there have always been periodic floods here.. could the severity of this one point to yet more evidence of a looming climate change crisis?

VO 29 The total cost is yet to be determined, but authorities fear its staggering.....and could cost the Western Cape a billion rand.

VO 30 Appeals are growing for the authorities to act… urgently, to mitigate people’s ever-growing risks to the ravages of climate change…

VO 31 Until then, communities like Citrusdal must rally to help each other.

UPSOUND: Riaan Carstens clip 4574 time code 11:49 we as a community need to pull together. Government resources can only help you so far, it’s the community that has to help itself.

VO 32 For Abrie, giving up is not an option.

UPSOUND Clip 4494 Time code: 08:11 We are strong. I think there is a long road ahead, but one makes a plan. Time code 09:10 We are strong, we believe in faith, that we will overcome, look to the future and make the best of a bad situation.
